source.title: Accelerating SGD with momentum for over-parameterized learning

record.tranche_reason: Compares optimizers using held-out image-classification accuracy, a different empirical test of optimizer generalization than the studies named in V4.
record.gate_note: The paper reports CIFAR-10 test accuracy for several optimizers. The synthetic-data convergence curves and training-loss curves do not measure the claim's train–test gap. V4 rows below retain the reported Adam and SGD test accuracies; Adam's table entries are associated with one learning-rate setting per architecture, while other Adam entries are blank.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares Adam, SGD and momentum SGD using CIFAR-10 held-out accuracy under limited hyperparameter tuning. These comparisons test V4, although optimizer generalization is secondary to the paper's optimization results.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the test-performance conclusion: MaSS has the highest reported CIFAR-10 accuracy on both architectures. The paper's central conclusion additionally concerns optimization: standard Nesterov SGD need not accelerate SGD, whereas MaSS has proven acceleration in the interpolating linear setting and favorable empirical convergence.
record.recipe_differences: Compares optimizers on CIFAR-10 CNN and ResNet-32 with data augmentation, learning-rate drops, and fixed epoch budgets; reports test accuracy rather than the train–test gap.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture and initial learning rate vary in the reported optimizer comparisons; the learning-rate schedules and epoch budgets are specified by architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: Theoretical and empirical batch-size regimes describe training convergence speed, including linear scaling, diminishing returns and saturation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing batch size yields diminishing gains in optimization speed beyond workload-dependent thresholds.

record.problems: The reported comparisons average 3 runs without an error bar. Adam is reported at only one initial step size, 0.001; the table does not report paired Adam results for the other listed learning rates. The results are test accuracy, not measured train–test gaps.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Held-out performance as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization on matched image tasks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Language benchmarks, broader optimizer tuning, decoupled weight decay and switching from Adam to SGD. Matched training performance is not established for the Table 1 comparisons.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Effects of varying dropout on held-out error; the architecture changes are not a controlled dropout comparison.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples compared with random removal.

missing.what: Plain SGD at initial learning rate 0.3: CNN test accuracy 82.41% and ResNet-32 test accuracy 92.51%. These comparisons preserve Adam's advantage on CNN but reverse it on ResNet-32.
SGD+Nesterov at the lower initial learning rates: CNN at 0.01 reaches 83.06%; ResNet-32 at 0.1 reaches 92.60%. Both outperform Adam.

At learning rate 0.3, SGD+Nesterov reaches 75.79% on CNN and 91.13% on ResNet-32, averaging only three convergent runs. It diverges in 5/8 CNN runs and 2/5 ResNet runs. These conditional accuracies and failure counts are needed to qualify comparisons favoring Adam at this setting.
missing.locator: Section 6, Table 1 footnote and following paragraph

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V4. A measured train–test gap is unnecessary for V4's held-out-performance comparison. Results average three runs without reported dispersion, so the accuracy differences are descriptive rather than established as statistically significant. The paper supplies two SGD learning rates per architecture but only Adam's default initial step size of 0.001; restricting the verdict to the extracted lower-rate SGD comparisons would omit results that change the conclusion.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization are not tested.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison for generalization.

Tests Adam against SGD on CIFAR-10 CNN and ResNet-32 at one reported initial learning-rate setting per architecture; does not test language benchmarks, broader hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching optimizers, or word-level language models.
Dropout is specified in some architecture details but is not varied to test its effect on held-out error.
No sharpness or other generalization measure is evaluated.
